airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway by being a discrete aircraft object rather than a long paved strip, from airport by lacking broad aviation-area context, and from industrial_area by lacking factory-like compounds and storage yards.
airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways and airport-related infrastructure, distinguishing airport from runway by broader aviation context, from airplane by lacking a single compact fuselage object, and from railway_station by lacking concentrated rail-line organization.
baseball_diamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield and surrounding outfield, distinguishing baseball_diamond from golf_course by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, from stadium by weaker enclosure and spectator structure, and from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated trailer-like housing rows.
basketball_court: small rectangular hard-court surface with clear sports markings, distinguishing basketball_court from tennis_court by court layout and line pattern, from parking_lot by lacking vehicle-row organization, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated roof-and-street neighborhood structure.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from island by lacking a fully isolated landmass, from desert by direct water contact, and from harbor by lacking dock-side port infrastructure.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from overpass by weaker elevated road-over-road structure, from harbor by lacking dock-and-shore maritime context, and from freeway by lacking a long continuous multi-lane corridor.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from desert by slightly richer vegetation texture, from mountain by weaker terrain relief, and from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy.
church: prominent religious building or complex with distinctive landmark-like architecture, distinguishing church from palace by less expansive ceremonial layout, from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns, and from commercial_area by weaker dense urban business-block organization.
circular_farmland: cultivated land with large regular circular irrigation patterns, distinguishing circular_farmland from rectangular_farmland by round parcel geometry, from storage_tank by broader agricultural texture around circles, and from wetland by lacking mixed water-vegetation fragmentation.
cloud: bright amorphous atmospheric mass with soft edges and no stable ground texture, distinguishing cloud from snowberg by weaker landform relief, from thermal_power_station by lacking heavy industrial structure, and from lake by lacking a stable enclosed water boundary.
commercial_area: dense urban business district with organized building blocks, roads, and large man-made structures, distinguishing commercial_area from industrial_area by lacking heavy factory compounds, from palace by weaker landmark-like symmetry, and from parking_lot by stronger building dominance rather than open paved vehicle space.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense_residential from medium_residential by much closer building intervals, from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row organization, and from commercial_area by smaller repeated residential roofs rather than larger business blocks.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from chaparral by weaker shrub texture, from mountain by less terrain relief, and from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular parcel boundaries, from wetland by weaker visible water fragmentation, and from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated residential rows.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous linear flow and road-network structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended roadway rather than a local elevated crossing, from runway by lacking aviation-strip context, and from intersection by lacking a compact junction node.
golf_course: large landscaped green field with fairways, lawns, and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golf_course from baseball_diamond by lacking a compact diamond infield, from runway by lacking a long straight paved strip, and from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy.
ground_track_field: sports venue with an oval running track and central field, distinguishing ground_track_field from stadium by weaker enclosure and spectator structure, from baseball_diamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield, and from tennis_court by lacking small repeated rectangular court geometry.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from ship by broader dock-and-shore context, from parking_lot by clear water-adjacent harbor organization, and from bridge by lacking a simple crossing structure.
industrial_area: large factory-like compounds with heavy infrastructure, storage yards, and production-oriented layouts, distinguishing industrial_area from parking_lot by stronger factory-compound structure, from storage_tank by not being dominated only by circular tanks, and from thermal_power_station by weaker power-plant-specific layout.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from roundabout by lacking a central circular traffic island, from overpass by weaker elevated overlap pattern, and from parking_lot by lacking organized vehicle-row layout.
island: landmass completely surrounded by water with clear shoreline boundary, distinguishing island from sea_ice by stable land texture rather than frozen surface, from beach by being an enclosed landform rather than a shoreline strip, and from lake by stronger land-water separation.
lake: large enclosed inland water body with smooth water surface and clear boundary, distinguishing lake from wetland by more uniform open water, from island by water-dominant appearance rather than land enclosed by water, and from river by lacking a strongly elongated channel shape.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries, from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, and from golf_course by weaker designed landscaping.
medium_residential: moderately spaced residential houses with visible yards and neighborhood streets, distinguishing medium_residential from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row structure, from dense_residential by larger spacing, and from sparse_residential by denser neighborhood grouping.
mobile_home_park: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobile_home_park from medium_residential by stronger trailer-like regularity, from dense_residential by more uniform layout, and from baseball_diamond by lacking sports-field geometry.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with strong relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from snowberg by less snow-dominant brightness, from desert by stronger terrain relief, and from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel structure.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its crossing and bridge-like form, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from bridge by emphasizing road-over-road transport structure.
palace: large landmark complex with symmetrical layout, open courtyards, and prominent architecture, distinguishing palace from church by more expansive ceremonial organization, from commercial_area by weaker dense urban block texture, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns.
parking_lot: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking_lot from industrial_area by lacking dense factory compounds, from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context, and from runway by lacking a long straight aviation strip.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from railway_station by lacking a concentrated station hub, from freeway by rail-line texture rather than paved multi-lane roadway, and from bridge by lacking a localized crossing structure.
railway_station: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railway_station from railway by stronger station-node organization, from industrial_area by clearer rail concentration, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip geometry and airport context.
rectangular_farmland: cultivated land divided into regular rectangular parcels, distinguishing rectangular_farmland from circular_farmland by angular field boundaries, from terrace by lacking stepped contour bands, and from meadow by stronger man-made agricultural organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from island by lacking a fully enclosed landmass, from wetland by showing a clearer continuous channel, and from lake by stronger linear flow shape.
roundabout: circular traffic junction with a central island and radiating roads, distinguishing roundabout from intersection by the visible circular center, from overpass by lacking a strong elevated crossing pattern, and from parking_lot by lacking organized vehicle rows.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open airport-like surroundings, distinguishing runway from airport by weaker terminal-scale context, from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body, and from freeway by lacking complex road branching.
sea_ice: bright frozen surface with irregular cracked or slab-like texture over water, distinguishing sea_ice from island by lacking stable land texture, from snowberg by flatter ice-field appearance, and from ship by lacking a discrete vessel shape.
ship: discrete vessel object on water with elongated hull-like structure, distinguishing ship from harbor by lacking broad dock-side context, from sea_ice by clear object boundaries and vessel shape, and from island by lacking stable landform texture.
snowberg: bright snow- or ice-covered elevated landform with strong cold-tone texture, distinguishing snowberg from mountain by stronger snow coverage, from sea_ice by stronger landform-like relief, and from cloud by more stable terrain-like structure.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse_residential from medium_residential by much larger spacing, from mobile_home_park by lacking uniform trailer-row organization, and from rectangular_farmland by repeated roof structures rather than crop parcels.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from baseball_diamond by larger scale, from ground_track_field by stronger venue framing, and from tennis_court by lacking small repeated rectangular courts.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage_tank from industrial_area by stronger circular-container dominance, from thermal_power_station by emphasizing tank clusters, and from church by lacking landmark-building structure.
tennis_court: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated court geometry, distinguishing tennis_court from basketball_court by different court layout and line pattern, from medium_residential by lacking roof clusters, and from industrial_area by lacking factory-compound structure.
terrace: stepped agricultural or hillside bands following slope contours, distinguishing terrace from rectangular_farmland by contour-aligned layered structure, from church by lacking landmark-building dominance, and from golf_course by lacking landscaped fairway organization.
thermal_power_station: large power-generation complex with heavy industrial structures, chimneys, or cooling-related facilities, distinguishing thermal_power_station from industrial_area by more plant-specific heavy layout, from storage_tank by broader power-plant infrastructure, and from cloud by stable man-made structure rather than amorphous atmospheric texture.
wetland: water-rich natural area with mixed shallow water and vegetation patches, distinguishing wetland from lake by more fragmented water-vegetation texture, from island by lacking a solid enclosed landmass, and from river by weaker continuous channel structure.
